elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 14: "Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, upon written notice to TrueLink". Client is our alias; the grant is direct and operative (the prior text only implied an election). No Order Forms exist in this agreement, so the Agreement-level grant is sufficient. Note the deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false; on inspection that is a false negative — the clause uses the defined alias "Client" and states no day-count, so the check appears keyed to the literal token "Customer" or to a numeric notice period.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 14 states no day-count; termination takes effect only when TrueLink stops services "until the last day of the month following the month of such notice", i.e. up to roughly 60 days (e.g. notice on 1 July → 31 August). To reach preferred the drafter must fix a flat effective date, e.g. "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice".

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 14 as rendered nor Section 5(a) contains any refund obligation. Section 5(a) says only that TrueLink invoices "on a monthly basis" and "Invoices will be paid within 15 days of receipt" — it does not state whether the monthly invoice is issued in advance or in arrears, so prepayment cannot be excluded. Preferred requires an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: As rendered, Section 14 grants a termination right only to Client. TrueLink's sole no-cause exit in Section 13 is non-renewal effective at the end of a one-year term ("TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days ... prior to the end of said year"). Section 13's automatic cut-off of Sections 2 and 3 is breach-triggered (Client breach of System/Credit Repository Agreements or Sections 8a–8c), i.e. for cause, not convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 14 as rendered gives Client an unqualified convenience right on written notice, with wind-down ending "the last day of the month following the month of such notice" — a determinate date of roughly 30–61 days, at or better than the 60–90 day band and well inside the 90-day ceiling. A shorter notice burden benefits us and is not a defect at this level. The "subject to Section 4 hereof" qualifier now attaches to TrueLink's continued-provision obligation, not to Client's right, so the grant itself is unconditional.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: no early-termination fee, penalty, unamortised charge or minimum-spend recapture appears in the cited or rendered text, and the redline introduces none. Fees are billed per Section 5(a) ("invoice ... on a monthly basis. Invoices will be paid within 15 days of receipt"), so nothing survives termination to be capped — a better outcome than the three-month cap. Residual open item: Section 4's blank minimum support period is not before us.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: TrueLink's only no-cause exit in the rendered text is the Section 13 notice "of intent not to renew ... prior to the end of said year", which operates only at the term boundary; Section 14 as recast confers no termination right on TrueLink. The stale "terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein" cross-reference does not create a vendor convenience exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 13 as amended: "TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days ... prior to the end of said year" — "no later than X days prior" is a minimum 90-day notice, replacing the former mutual thirty (30) days that sat in the walk-away band. Client's own 30-day non-renewal notice is preserved.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: all four fallback elements are met in operative language, so the claimed target is supported and the "deviation" finding is correctly resolved to the fallback. Preferred is correctly not claimed.

Preferred fails on two elements: (i) Section 14 fixes no 30-day effective date (the month-end-following mechanic can run ~60 days) and (ii) there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. To reach preferred, amend Section 14 to read "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice" and add "TrueLink shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination."

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" (ok=false) is a false negative on the substance: the rendered Section 14 expressly grants "Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, upon written notice". The check appears keyed to the literal alias "Customer" or to an explicit numeric notice period, neither of which appears; no repair is required at the fallback level.

Minimal: only two edits were made — recasting Section 14 into a direct grant while keeping the existing wind-down date and the Section 4 qualifier, and splitting Section 13's mutual non-renewal notice into Client 30 days / TrueLink 90 days. Favourable existing language (Client's 30-day non-renewal, the wind-down obligation, ownership of domains, migration windows) is retained, no operative term is duplicated, and nothing outside the T4C checklist is added.

Preserves intent: payment mechanics (Section 5(a) monthly invoicing, 15-day payment), the one-year term and auto-renewal, the cause-based cut-off of Sections 2 and 3, and the name-server/hosting migration obligations all survive without contradiction.

Follow-up tidy-ups (do not block this pass, but should be repaired in a clean-up round): (a) Section 13's "terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein" is a stale cross-reference — termination is Section 14 — and left uncorrected it creates a needless argument that early termination is limited to a section that contains no termination right; change it to "Section 14" or add "unless earlier terminated in accordance with Section 14" to the term sentence. (b) Confirm the blank minimum support period in Section 4 does not reintroduce a commitment that could be read to fetter the new convenience right; if it does, qualify Section 14 with "Notwithstanding Section 4".
